gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-sahitya: Sahitya is a text serif whose thin strokes sit only a hair under the thick ones, with uncrowded mouths on its s and c. Bellota Text above it keeps every word at a flat, unvarying weight.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-sawarabi-mincho: Sawarabi Mincho brings classic serif manners, with terminals cut short of the bowl and joins that ease only slightly. Its bends taper mildly, while Bellota Text draws every curve with no stress at all.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-sedan: Sedan is a text serif with a mellow range of weights, like a dip pen used gently, its terminals held far from the stroke. And Bellota Text sets against it a ribbon of constant width, which is the sharpest difference here.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-sedan-sc: Bellota Text draws its letters with essentially zero stroke contrast, open on the c and s, so the headings look smooth and drawn from one line. But Sedan SC, a classic serif, carries a modest thick-thin shift that keeps a long page lively.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-shippori-mincho: Distinctive in its flat, uncalligraphic lettering, Bellota Text leads, while Shippori Mincho, a classic serif, adds a gentle modulation you notice on close look. That keeps paragraphs comfortable.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-shippori-mincho-b: Shippori Mincho B1 reads refined, with a crescent-wide c and hairlines sturdy enough to hold up, as a classic serif should. Over many lines its medium contrast never turns sharp.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-stix-two-text: STIX Two Text reads editorial and traditional, its thins only slightly lighter than its thicks and its terminals pulled back from each curve. STIX Two Text swells and tapers gently along those curves, so a long page moves smoothly beneath the stroke-flat heading.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-tai-heritage-pro: Tai Heritage Pro is a dignified classic serif with a clear channel leading into each round letter. And Bellota Text, with its tube-like constant stroke, makes the body's sturdy downstrokes and slender turns feel comfortably varied.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-taviraj: Bellota Text looks like glass tubing bent into letters, with open curves and no calligraphic shading anywhere. Taviraj, a classic serif, keeps stems a little heavier than its hairlines and leaves a generous gap where each curve ends, so extended reading stays easy.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-trirong: Bellota Text has no modulation between stems and connecting strokes, so its open c, e and s shapes look drawn in one go. And Trirong, a text serif, uses a tempered contrast that neither jolts nor flattens over a full page.
